seo.title: Freight Bill Audit for Manufacturers | VipraTech
seo.description: Audit transporter bills against contracted lane rates, LRs, PODs and weights, and catch duplicate bills, wrong detention and surcharges before payment.

problem.intro: Manufacturers of fertilisers, cement, chemicals, steel and packaged goods pay thousands of transporter bills a month, each with a lane rate, a vehicle type, a weight or trip basis and extras for detention, loading, unloading, tolls and fuel. Contracts change every quarter or with diesel prices. Most bills are checked by sampling, and overcharges are paid in full.

pain_points.title: Rates from an old contract
pain_points.detail: Bills use a lane rate or diesel adjustment that no longer applies, and nobody checks every bill against the current contract.

pain_points.title: Billed weight above moved weight
pain_points.detail: Bills charge the vehicle capacity or a rounded weight instead of the weight on the weighbridge slip.

pain_points.title: Detention and extras without proof
pain_points.detail: Detention, multi-point delivery and loading charges are added without the gate times or approvals that justify them.

pain_points.title: Duplicate and split bills
pain_points.detail: The same LR is billed twice, or one trip is split across two bills.

solution.overview: VipraTech reads each transporter bill and its LRs, PODs and weighbridge slips, and recalculates the charge from the contract in force on the dispatch date: lane, vehicle type, basis, minimum load and fuel adjustment. Detention is recalculated from gate-in and gate-out times against free time, and every extra needs its approval or proof. Duplicate LRs are caught across bills and months. Lines that pass go to a payment sheet; the rest go to logistics with the recalculation.
capabilities: Recalculates each bill from the contract in force on the dispatch date
Checks billed weight against weighbridge slips and minimum load terms
Recalculates detention from gate times and free time
Checks extras such as loading, tolls and multi-point delivery against approvals
Catches duplicate and split bills across transporters and months
Shows overcharges and cost per tonne by lane and transporter

workflow.title: Receive bills
workflow.detail: Transporter bills arrive with LRs and PODs, by upload, email or portal.

workflow.title: Read and link
workflow.detail: Each bill line is linked to its LR, POD, weighbridge slip and dispatch.

workflow.title: Recalculate
workflow.detail: Freight is recalculated from the contract, weight and fuel adjustment in force.

workflow.title: Check extras
workflow.detail: Detention and extras are checked against gate times and approvals.

workflow.title: Review
workflow.detail: Overcharged and doubtful lines go to logistics with the recalculation.

workflow.title: Pay
workflow.detail: Accounts payable pays the approved amount and sends the transporter a statement.

match_rules.rule: Contract rate on the dispatch date
match_rules.logic: The rate is taken from the contract version in force on the dispatch date for that lane, vehicle type and basis.
Per-tonne bills use the weighbridge weight, or the contract minimum load where it is higher. Rounded or capacity weights are corrected.
Diesel adjustments follow the contract formula and the index value for the period.
Detention is paid only for time beyond free time, from gate-in and gate-out records, at the contract rate.
An LR can be billed once. Split bills for one trip and repeated LRs across months are held.

exception_codes.meaning: The billed rate differs from the contract for that lane and date.
Billed weight is above the weighbridge weight.
Detention has no gate times or is within free time.
exception_codes.action: Remove it unless proof is added.

exception_codes.meaning: An extra charge has no approval.
exception_codes.action: Ask logistics to approve or remove it.
Reject, with the earlier bill linked.

exception_codes.meaning: No proof of delivery for the trip.
exception_codes.action: Hold payment until the POD arrives.

inputs: Lorry receipts and proofs of delivery
Weighbridge slips and gate-in and gate-out records
Freight contracts, lane rates and fuel adjustment formula
outputs: Every bill line recalculated with the difference
Exceptions with reason codes and evidence
Cost per tonne and overcharge rate by lane and transporter
human_in_the_loop: Logistics decides every disputed line and every extra without approval. Accounts payable releases payment only for approved amounts.
integrations: ERP such as SAP or Oracle for dispatches and payables
Transport management system or LR register
Transporter portal or email for bills
guardrails: Contract version applied by dispatch date
No payment without a POD unless logistics approves
Duplicate LRs held across all transporters
Every reduction shown with the clause behind it
compliance_notes: Transporter bills may involve GST under reverse charge or forward charge; the system keeps the tax fields from each bill for accounts payable.

rollout.scope: One plant or region, using the last two months of transporter bills, with paid amounts as the benchmark.

what_we_measure.how: Share of bill lines recalculated, not sampled.
Amount billed above the contract, confirmed by logistics.

faqs.q: Our contracts change with diesel prices. Can it keep up?
faqs.a: Yes. The fuel adjustment formula is set up once, and each bill uses the index value for its period.

faqs.q: Transporters send bills as PDFs and scans. Is that a problem?
faqs.a: No. Bills, LRs and PODs are read into structured lines, and anything read with low confidence is shown to a person.
Yes. Railway receipts and freight charges are checked the same way, with the rail rate basis set up as rules.

faqs.q: Can it show which transporters overcharge most?
faqs.a: Yes. Overcharge rates by transporter and lane come with every cycle.
